picks.matchup: San Francisco 49ers vs Las Vegas Raiders
picks.analysis: Klint Kubiak's Raiders host the 49ers in a meaningful home showcase for a franchise in the first year of a new era. Las Vegas will be without starting RG Jackson Powers-Johnson (ankle, confirmed out Thursday) and WR Dont'e Thornton, who has missed over a week of practice and also won't play. Caleb Rogers steps in at guard and Noah Brown gets elevated WR reps. The depth concerns are real — this mirrors Powers-Johnson's injury-plagued 2025 — but the 49ers are a road preseason visitor unlikely to extend their starters far, and the Raiders' home edge at -2.5 is enough in this spot.

picks.matchup: Los Angeles Rams vs Los Angeles Chargers
picks.analysis: The biggest story of Preseason Week 3: Justin Herbert makes his first-ever preseason appearance at SoFi Stadium. Drafted in the COVID year of 2020, Herbert has never once suited up for an exhibition game — and it was Herbert himself who walked up to Jim Harbaugh and asked to play, saying he needed to feel a live pass rush. Harbaugh is going with his offensive starters while sitting Derwin James Jr. and Khalil Mack on defense. A fired-up Herbert running a live first-team offense against a Rams unit unlikely to counter with full starters makes the Chargers' 4.5-point cushion very manageable.

picks.analysis: Dan Quinn's Commanders head into Baltimore with a battered roster: DT Daron Payne is out, DT Johnny Newton has a long-term injury, C Nick Allegretti remains sidelined with a calf issue forcing rookie Matt Gulbin into center reps, RB Jerome Ford was released with an injury settlement, and RB Rachaad White is limited. The Ravens have their own OL instability — starting center Danny Pinter suffered a season-ending training camp injury and veteran Ethan Pocic has been elevated to first-team center. With both teams patchwork up front and the Ravens likely managing Lamar Jackson's workload, taking Washington at +3.5 offers real value.

picks.matchup: New York Giants vs New York Jets
picks.analysis: John Harbaugh's Giants arrive at MetLife riding a dominant 26-3 preseason dismantling of Miami, with coaches singling out sixth-round rookie OL J.C. Davis for playing a complete game at left tackle and grading out well. WR Malik Nabers shedding his red non-contact jersey is described as 'a possibility' this week, adding intrigue to the crosstown rivalry. Aaron Glenn's Jets have been playing all available personnel for evaluation throughout the preseason — a strategy that works for roster-building but leaves them short against a more structured Giants squad that looks further along in installing Harbaugh's culture.

picks.analysis: Nick Sirianni's Eagles host the Bengals at home. The Bengals played Joe Burrow and their starters in their preseason opener earlier this month, and by Week 3 Zac Taylor will be protecting his veterans as the regular season approaches — expect backups to carry the bulk of Cincinnati's offensive load. Philadelphia at home with their own deeper roster, the crowd behind them, and the advantage of familiarity from the earlier meeting gives the Eagles the edge at -2.5.

picks.analysis: Caleb Williams looked rough in Preseason Week 2 against the Bengals — just 2-of-5 for 27 yards with a 58.8 passer rating on a single drive. Ben Johnson has since signaled he will limit Williams' exposure in Week 3, preferring to give him joint-practice reps against the Titans on Thursday rather than game action Saturday, leaving backup Case Keenum to carry the bulk of the load. Robert Saleh's Titans at home against a Bears team operating primarily with backups is the definition of a comfortable cover.
